audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer spikes are generic Graves boilerplate ('Levels 1-3 and your first item'), and phases[4] describes Collateral Damage as an execute-plus-knockback rather than as the Level 6 all-in that must beat Wither to the punch.
audit.why: The real spike order in this lane is: Level 3 with a Quickdraw charge against a Wither-less Nasus, Level 6 with a full magazine, and the first-item spike — after which Nasus' stacks and Spirit Fire shred pass Graves permanently. Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s, so the punish windows are timed off it, not off Graves' own pattern.
audit.corrected: phases[2], [4], [5] and [6] rewritten to the real spike order and keyed to Wither's cooldown.
sources: enemyKit E Spirit Fire armor reduction

audit.whatIsWrong: content 'early' states: 'Smoke Screen (W) blinds his Siphoning Strike (it's an empowered auto, so the blind makes it miss)'. report[10].t and phases[6].why also call the W a blind.
audit.why: Riot's text for Graves' W is 'creating a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range' plus impact damage and a brief slow — it is a nearsight and a slow, with no blind component; the kit flags are projectile, slow, zone only. The mirror audit on nasus__graves flags this as the single highest-value error in the matchup. Telling a Graves player his W makes a stacked Siphoning Strike whiff will get him killed by the one ability he most needs to dodge.
audit.corrected: Smoke Screen reduces sight range and slows on impact; a stacked Siphoning Strike lands inside it normally. Use it to break his vision, not to make his Q miss.
sources: ownerKit W Riot text and flags

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing states that Graves' attacks fire 4 bullets which cannot pass through units.
audit.why: Riot's passive text is explicit. Nasus only has to keep a minion between himself and Graves for the volley to be eaten entirely — the mirror audit records this from his side, so it must appear from Graves' side as the reason half-range trades through the wave do nothing.
audit.corrected: Stated in dontsFull[0].d: the four bullets cannot pass through units, so a minion in the way eats the volley.

audit.whatIsWrong: End of the Line's terrain behaviour is described as a 'wall-bounce return', which is not what Riot's text says.
audit.why: Riot: 'fires an explosive shell that detonates after 1 second, or after colliding with terrain.' Terrain makes it detonate EARLY — there is no return hit in the description. The mirror audit states the same thing from Nasus' side.
audit.corrected: phases[2].why now says End of the Line detonates early off a wall.

edits.before: Nasus is weak and stack-hungry early, so this is your window — but respect Wither (W) the second he hits 2. Until then, Quickdraw (E) in for the point-blank 4-shell spread and drop an End of the Line (Q) cone to deny his Siphoning Strike last-hits and zone him off the wave. Do NOT linger in auto range once his W is up: Wither slows your move speed AND attack speed, which kills your kite, your reload tempo and your shell DPS at once. Smoke Screen (W) blinds his Siphoning Strike (it's an empowered auto, so the blind makes it miss) and slows him, but it does nothing to remove the Wither slow already on you.
edits.after: Nasus is weak and stack-hungry early, so this is your window — but respect Wither (W) the second he hits 2. Until then, Quickdraw (E) in for the point-blank 4-shell spread and drop an End of the Line (Q) cone to deny his Siphoning Strike last-hits and zone him off the wave. Do NOT linger in auto range once his W is up: Wither slows your move speed AND attack speed, which kills your kite, your reload tempo and your shell DPS at once. Smoke Screen (W) does not blind — it reduces sight range and slows on impact, so a stacked Siphoning Strike still lands inside it. Use it to break his sight of you while you reload, never as a way to make his Q miss.

notes: Highest-value fix confirmed against the mirror (nasus__graves): content 'early' told the player Smoke Screen blinds Siphoning Strike and makes it whiff. Riot's W text is 'reduces sight range' plus a brief slow — there is no blind, and a stacked Q lands inside the smoke normally. The same false claim leaked into report[10].t ('W smoke blinds tower dives') and phases[6].why ('smoke-screen blinds'); all three are corrected here and now agree with the Nasus-side page. Level chart: the content win[] and the full-layer phases disagreed with each other AND with the packet, while the content whys matched the packet exactly — I flipped both charts to the packet order as one atomic group so the two directions and the two layers agree. Note the brief's top-level 'games: 1924' disagrees with packet.games 34; I used the packet figure and the packet win rate, which is the Emerald+ number. Nothing about tenacity, cleanse or QSS against Wither is asserted — not in Riot's text, so left unstated.
